SELECT c.name, 0 AS total_orders FROM customers c WHERE 0 GROUP BY c.name;
lessons.solution_code: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.name;

mastery_exam.question: Which SQL clause filters grouped rows after aggregation?
mastery_exam.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters after aggregation.

mastery_exam.question: Type keyword to remove duplicate rows: SELECT ___ country FROM customers;
mastery_exam.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result.
